stories.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5 to the public and Mythos 5 to trusted cyber partners

key_facts.fact: Anthropic on June 9, 2026 launched Claude Fable 5, its first Mythos-class model cleared for general use, alongside Claude Mythos 5, the same underlying model with cyber safeguards lifted and available only to a small group of vetted cyberdefenders through Project Glasswing.
key_facts.excerpt: Today we're launching Claude Fable 5: a Mythos-class model that we've made safe for general use.

key_facts.fact: Fable 5 ships with classifiers that route queries on cybersecurity, biology/chemistry, and model distillation to the earlier Claude Opus 4.8 model, with the user notified; Anthropic says fallback triggers in fewer than 5% of sessions.
key_facts.excerpt: Unlike Mythos 5, though, the publicly accessible Fable 5 is designed to funnel queries on certain sensitive topics to the earlier Claude Opus 4.8 model and to warn the user when this is happening.

key_facts.fact: Mythos 5 scored 78% on the ExploitBench cybersecurity benchmark, nearly double Claude Opus 4.8's 40% and above the 69% from the earlier Mythos Preview.
key_facts.excerpt: Mythos 5 scored a 78 percent on the benchmark's tests of vulnerable code exploits, a significant increase from the 40 percent score from Opus 4.8, and even the 69 percent score achieved by Mythos Preview.

key_facts.fact: On Vellum's breakdown, Fable 5 scored 80.3% on SWE-Bench Pro versus 69.2% for Opus 4.8 and 58.6% for GPT-5.5, and ranks #1 on the Hebbia Finance senior-analyst benchmark.
key_facts.excerpt: On June 9, 2026, Anthropic released Claude Fable 5: the first model from its 'Mythos-class' tier, the level that now sits above the Opus class, that it has cleared for general use.

key_facts.fact: After more than 1,000 hours of red-team testing through an external bug bounty, Anthropic says no universal jailbreaks were found for Fable 5.
key_facts.excerpt: In over 1,000 hours of red-team testing with a bug bounty program, Anthropic says external teams failed to find any universal jailbreaks for Fable 5.

key_facts.fact: Fable 5 API pricing is $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, roughly 2x Claude Opus 4.8 input and roughly 2x GPT-5.5 sticker input price.
key_facts.excerpt: The API price is $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, which is 2x the cost of Claude Opus 4.8 and 2x GPT-5.5's input price on sticker.

key_facts.fact: Fable 5 is included on Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans at no extra cost through June 22, 2026, after which usage credits will be required.
key_facts.excerpt: Subscription plans (Pro, Max, Team, seat-based Enterprise): Included at no extra cost through June 22, 2026. Usage credits required after June 23.

stories.headline: Trump administration tells CAISI to stop publishing AI model evaluations

key_facts.fact: Trump administration officials told the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) to halt publication of its frontier AI model assessments while the June 2 executive order is implemented, the Wall Street Journal first reported.
key_facts.excerpt: According to The Wall Street Journal (WSJ) on Monday, the Trump administration directed the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) to halt the issuance of evaluation reports. The directive applies while the executive order President Trump signed last week remains in effect.

key_facts.fact: National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross directly ordered CAISI to stop publishing its model assessments, citing national security concerns; the directive does not end CAISI's testing or its voluntary agreements with AI developers, only the public output.
key_facts.excerpt: National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross directed the Center for AI Standards and Innovation, known as CAISI, to cease issuing public reports on its assessments of advanced AI models, citing national-security concerns.

key_facts.fact: The June 2, 2026 executive order creates a voluntary framework for AI companies to share frontier models with the federal government up to 30 days before public release to 'promote secure innovation and strengthen the cybersecurity of critical infrastructure.'
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump signed an executive order Tuesday creating a 'voluntary framework' for AI companies to share their frontier models with the federal government before they're released ... the current version asks companies to share their models up to 30 days before public release.

key_facts.fact: The order assigns the classified benchmarking process to the Treasury Department, the NSA and CISA, with the NSA director determining when a model qualifies as a 'covered frontier model.'
key_facts.excerpt: the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of War, through the Director of NSA, and the Secretary of Homeland Security, through the Director of CISA ... develop and maintain a classified benchmarking process to assess the advanced cyber capabilities of AI models.

key_facts.fact: Within the agency, the halt drew criticism as an attempt by Cairncross to widen his influence over evaluations; OpenAI raised CAISI's importance with the administration, while White House AI advisers including David Sacks have warned that excessive verification could slow deployment.
key_facts.excerpt: Within the agency, the halt to CAISI's public activities has drawn negative views over Director Cairncross's attempt to exert more influence in the evaluation process ... companies such as OpenAI have discussed CAISI's importance with the administration. White House AI advisers, including venture capitalist David Sacks, have warned that excessive model verification could slow deployment.

stories.headline: EU orders Meta to give rival AI chatbots free access to WhatsApp via emergency interim measure

key_facts.fact: The European Commission on June 9 ordered Meta to give competing AI assistants free access to WhatsApp under emergency interim measures while it completes an antitrust investigation, the second time the EU has used the emergency power in over 20 years
key_facts.excerpt: The European Commission ordered Meta on Tuesday to give competing artificial intelligence assistants free access to WhatsApp, a rare emergency intervention that will stay in force until it completes an antitrust investigation into the company... It is the second time the Commission has used the emergency power in more than two decades.

key_facts.fact: Meta has until June 15 to restore rivals' access to the WhatsApp for Business API on the same terms that applied before October 2025, when it began restricting AI rivals while exempting its own Meta AI assistant
key_facts.excerpt: Meta has until June 15th to comply... Meta later restored access to rival chatbots 'for a fee' in March, seemingly in violation of EU competition rules. Now, the Commission is ordering Meta to reinstate WhatsApp access for third-party AI rivals under the same terms and conditions that were in place before the ban, which was 'notably free of charge.'

key_facts.fact: If Meta ignores the order it could face fines of up to 10% of annual global revenue, or roughly $20 billion based on its 2025 earnings; the interim measure can last until June 2029 or until the investigation concludes
key_facts.excerpt: If Meta ignores the order, it could face fines of up to 10 percent of annual revenue, or around $20 billion, based on 2025 earnings.

key_facts.fact: The investigation followed complaints from The Interaction Company of California (developer of Poke.com), French AI startup Agentik and a Spanish rival; Meta said it will appeal, calling it 'regulatory overreach'
key_facts.excerpt: The European Commission's decision to issue an interim measure against Meta followed complaints from The Interaction Company of California, developer of the Poke.com AI assistant, French AI startup Agentik and a Spanish rival... 'The European Commission has decided that OpenAI and some of the largest companies in the world can use the paid-for WhatsApp Business product for free,' a Meta spokesperson said.

key_facts.fact: Italy folded its near-identical probe into the EU investigation a day before the decision; Brazil's regulator had already forced Meta to reopen access there in March
key_facts.excerpt: Italy and Brazil have pursued near-identical cases, with the Italian competition authority folding its probe into the EU investigation a day before Tuesday's decision and Brazil's forcing Meta to reopen access there in March.

stories.headline: Google launches Gemini 3.5 Live Translate, a real-time speech-to-speech model covering 70+ languages

key_facts.fact: Google on June 9, 2026 released Gemini 3.5 Live Translate, an audio-to-audio model that auto-detects more than 70 languages and generates continuously streamed translated speech preserving the speaker's intonation, pacing and pitch.
key_facts.excerpt: Gemini 3.5 Live Translate is our latest audio model, delivering near real-time speech-to-speech translation in over 70 languages.

key_facts.fact: Unlike turn-based systems, the model speaks continuously and stays just a few seconds behind the original speaker, avoiding the long pauses traditional speech translation produces.
key_facts.excerpt: Unlike turn by turn systems that wait for the speaker to finish speaking before responding, 3.5 Live Translate generates speech continuously, balancing the trade-off between waiting for context to improve quality and translating immediately to stay in sync with the speaker.

key_facts.fact: It is rolling out today in the Google Translate app on Android and iOS, in public preview for developers through the Gemini Live API and Google AI Studio, and in private preview to select Google Workspace customers via Google Meet.
key_facts.excerpt: For developers in public preview via the Gemini Live API and Google AI Studio; For enterprises in private preview starting this month in Google Meet; For everyone via Google Translate on Android and iOS

key_facts.fact: In Google Meet the model raises supported languages from 5 to 70+, enabling more than 2,000 language combinations in a single meeting, versus the prior limit of translating only to and from English.
key_facts.excerpt: Speech translation in the video calling app previously supported just five languages. The model's support for 70+ languages unlocks '2000+ language combinations in one meeting, expanding from the previous state of only translating to and from English.'

key_facts.fact: The Translate Android app also gains a new 'listening mode' that pipes translations through the phone's earpiece without headphones, treating the device like a regular call.
key_facts.excerpt: The Android app is also rolling out a new 'listening mode' that lets you hear translations through the phone's earpiece when you don't have headphones immediately available.

key_facts.fact: The developer model code is gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview with an input token limit of 131,072 and output token limit of 65,536; audio output is watermarked with SynthID.
key_facts.excerpt: Model code gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview ... Input token limit 131,072 Output token limit 65,536

stories.headline: Seattle City Council votes 9-0 for one-year moratorium on new large data centers

key_facts.fact: The Seattle City Council voted unanimously on June 9 to impose a one-year emergency moratorium on new large data centers inside city limits.
key_facts.excerpt: The Seattle City Council voted unanimously Tuesday to impose a one-year emergency moratorium on new large data centers inside the city limits, responding to concerns about the implications of AI for the city's power grid, water supply, utility rates, and economy.

key_facts.fact: The ordinance halts applications for data centers with electrical capacity above 20 megavolt-amperes (roughly 20 MW), enough power for thousands of homes.
key_facts.excerpt: The council approved two measures: an ordinance halting applications for data centers with electrical capacity of more than 20 megavolt-amperes — enough power for thousands of homes — and a resolution committing the city to study their impacts as a precursor to permanent regulations.

key_facts.fact: Mayor Katie Wilson is expected to sign the legislation; the moratorium can be extended for an additional six months and a public hearing must be held within 60 days.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the legislation, data centers are defined as facilities used primarily to store and process digital data, with power capacity exceeding 20 megavolt-amperes and requiring uninterrupted power service. The moratorium could be extended for an additional six months if necessary.

key_facts.fact: Proposed data center projects in Seattle reportedly had combined peak demand equal to about a third of the city's average daily power consumption.
key_facts.excerpt: The moratorium would take effect as soon as Mayor Katie Wilson signs it, temporarily halting projects like several large data centers that companies have approached Seattle City Light about building in the city. Those projects reportedly had a combined peak demand equal to about a third of Seattle's average daily power consumption.

key_facts.fact: The ordinance exempts roughly 30 smaller data centers already operating in Seattle, allowing each to expand by up to another 20 megavolt-amperes.
key_facts.excerpt: The ordinance exempts the roughly 30 smaller data centers already operating in Seattle, allowing each to expand by up to another 20 megavolt-amperes, which is the same amount as the threshold of the moratorium on new facilities.

stories.headline: SoftBank's $6B margin loan against its OpenAI stake stalls with creditors

key_facts.fact: SoftBank Group's talks with potential creditors to raise at least $6 billion through a margin loan backed by its OpenAI stake have stalled, Bloomberg reported, weeks after SoftBank cut the target from an original $10 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: SoftBank Group's talks with potential creditors to raise at least $6 billion from a margin loan backed by its OpenAI stake have stalled, people familiar with the matter said, just weeks after the Japanese conglomerate cut its initial target from $10 billion.

key_facts.fact: Before the talks stalled, SoftBank had secured roughly $5 billion in commitments, though it was unclear whether those were verbal or written.
key_facts.excerpt: SoftBank had secured some $5 billion for the loan before the development, people familiar with the matter said, though it was unclear if those were verbal or written commitments.

key_facts.fact: Lenders balked at valuing exposure tied to OpenAI, which is private, and reportedly cited reports of OpenAI missing some internal sales and user milestones in recent quarters; the loan was structured with a two-year term and a one-year extension option.
key_facts.excerpt: Some prospective creditors balked at the problem of valuing OpenAI, a private company, as collateral, and at reports that the startup has missed some internal sales and user milestones in recent quarters. The loan was structured with a two-year term and a one-year extension option.

key_facts.fact: The stalled talks come one day after OpenAI said it had confidentially filed for a US IPO; SoftBank also still faces a $40 billion bridge loan repayment due in 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The funding delay comes a day after OpenAI said it had confidentially filed for a US initial public offering (IPO) ... it still faces a $40 billion bridge loan repayment due in 2027, adding to financing pressure.

key_facts.fact: SoftBank says it is considering various fundraising options and could still revive the margin loan at a later stage.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is considering various fundraising options, according to the people, who asked not to be identified discussing private matters. It could still move forward with the margin loan at a later stage, they added.

stories.headline: Tata chairman says TCS will soon have as many AI agents as its 600,000 employees, hiring to slow

key_facts.fact: Tata chairman Natarajan Chandrasekaran said at TCS's June 9 annual general meeting that the IT services giant will soon have as many AI agents as human employees, with the company plans to reduce hiring as AI use accelerates
key_facts.excerpt: Tata chairman Natarajan Chandrasekaran said TCS, Asia's biggest software services firm, plans to reduce hiring in the coming years as it steps up the use of AI... 'The company will have an equal number of AI workers — we call them AI agents — as there are employees,' Chandrasekaran said. 'If the company has half a million employees, the day is not far when the company will have half a million AI agents.'

key_facts.fact: TCS is India's largest private-sector employer with around 600,000 staff; its headcount fell by more than 23,000 on a net basis in fiscal year ended March 2026, after cutting more than 12,000 jobs in July 2025
key_facts.excerpt: Mumbai-headquartered TCS does not plan to downsize staff, but will hire less, Chandrasekaran said. Last July, it cut more than 12,000 jobs, while headcount fell by more than 23,000 on a net basis in the fiscal year ended March 2026.

key_facts.fact: Chandrasekaran predicted TCS will reach AI-agent-to-employee parity within three years and said 100% of TCS revenue will have an AI component before the end of the decade
key_facts.excerpt: 'I predict that over the next three years, TCS will have as many AI agents as human employees.'... The Tata Sons chairman also disclosed that TCS had an annualised AI revenue run-rate of $2.4 billion in the last quarter of fiscal 2026, growing at a compound quarterly growth rate of 22.4%.

key_facts.fact: TCS reported an annualized AI revenue run-rate of $2.4 billion in Q4 fiscal 2026, growing at a 22.4% compound quarterly rate, against the backdrop of India's $315 billion IT services sector
key_facts.excerpt: India's $315-billion IT sector has been grappling with investor concerns that AI could disrupt its traditional, labour-intensive business model.

stories.headline: Reuters: Trump family banked $2.3B from four crypto ventures while investors lost the same amount

key_facts.fact: A Reuters investigation found the Trump family generated about $2.3 billion in pretax income from four crypto ventures between November 2024 and April 2026, while more than one million investors absorbed about $2.3 billion in net losses
key_facts.excerpt: A Reuters investigation found the Trump family generated at least $2.3 billion from four crypto ventures since returning to the White House, while more than a million investors lost the same amount on the other side of those trades.

key_facts.fact: World Liberty Financial was the largest contributor, channeling more than $1.4 billion to the family through a structure giving DT Marks DEFI LLC a 75% cut of token sale proceeds; WLFI holders sat on roughly $674 million in losses by end of April
key_facts.excerpt: World Liberty Financial accounted for the largest share of the Trump family's reported crypto revenue... DT Marks DEFI LLC, a corporate entity linked to the family, secured a contractual right to 75% of token sale proceeds after expenses, generating an estimated $987 million for the family. However, the token Buyers faced a different outcome. World Liberty investors were sitting on roughly $674 million in losses by the end of April.

key_facts.fact: The TRUMP meme coin generated roughly $616 million for the family while buyers lost more than $700 million; ALT5 Sigma shareholders lost about $675 million and American Bitcoin investors lost over $200 million
key_facts.excerpt: On the investor side, WLFI token holders absorbed approximately $674 million in losses. $TRUMP coin investors lost more than $700 million. Purchasers of ALT5 Sigma shares recorded losses of around $675 million. And American Bitcoin investors faced over $200 million in losses.

key_facts.fact: Reuters found no evidence the Trumps invested their own capital; experts said each venture could have been set up for under $1 million in development and legal costs, with gains coming from licensing and revenue sharing
key_facts.excerpt: In each case, the Trumps licensed the family name rather than investing their own capital, promoted the ventures through social media and public appearances, and collected revenue as investors piled in... Experts said each venture could have been established for less than $1 million in development and legal costs, meaning the family's $2.3 billion gain came almost entirely from licensing fees and revenue sharing rather than capital at risk.

key_facts.fact: Eight government ethics experts told Reuters the arrangement represents a conflict of interest unlike anything seen in modern American history, though all noted it is legal absent a quid pro quo
key_facts.excerpt: Eight government ethics experts told Reuters the arrangement represents a conflict of interest unlike anything seen in modern American history... All eight noted the conduct is legal provided no regulatory favors are exchanged for financial gain.
